title: The extracted structure of a parking sign
description: The contract between the vision model and the deterministic code. The model fills in ONLY these fields: a closed list, with additionalProperties forbidden everywhere. Anything the model would like to say beyond the schema goes into notes and does not enter the computation.

main_sign.description: The top panel of the stack. NOT part of panels: in a probe the model duplicated the P as a first plate, so validation must discard a panel whose entire content is the main sign's pictogram.

type.description: wayfinding_* permit no parking at all - they are direction signs, and must not be confused with a sign that permits parking.

form.description: zone marks the start of a zone (a yellow square with a round sign inside). The rule reads the same as on an ordinary sign; the product does not compute how far the zone extends.

panels.description: The panels BELOW the main sign, strictly in top-to-bottom order. The order matters: the rule depends on it.

panel_count.description: The number of panels below the main sign. Deliberately duplicates the length of panels: a disagreement signals that the model lost a boundary, and it cannot be derived from the list itself.

boundaries.description: About the boundaries between panels. The model STATES its opinion here, but the code does not take it on trust: on photograph 013 two plates were merged into one with certain = true. Uncertainty is assembled by code from independent signals.

doubt.description: Between which adjacent panels the boundary is in doubt. Panel indices.

notes.description: Free text from the model. Does NOT enter the engine or the confidence formula: prose is not checked by code. It exists so the model has somewhere to put an observation for which there is no field, and so such observations stay visible when errors are examined.

model_confidence.description: The model's own estimate. One of the inputs to the confidence formula, and not the deciding one.

color.description: Background colour is an extracted field, not decoration. In Sweden warning and prohibition signs are yellow, so a yellow panel means a prohibition or a restriction; blue and white sit under permitting signs.

legibility.description: Legibility as a schema field rather than a phrase in notes: the confidence formula works with fields, not with prose.

index.description: Position from the top, starting at 1.

kind.description: What kind of panel this is. `sign_plate` - a plate that states a rule: only these reach the engine. `operator_plate` - a plate carrying an operator's name and telephone: in form a lawful additional plate, but it states no rule. `info_board` - a payment board with a zone code and app advertising, which is not a road sign at all. The last two are marked rather than discarded: they are visible in the photograph, and passing over them silently looks like a loss. They do not reach the user's answer.

lines.description: The text verbatim, line by line, in Swedish, with brackets and hyphens as on the sign. An empty array if the panel carries only a pictogram.

parsed.description: The second layer: what the model assigned to known categories. The fields are independent and all optional - one panel usually carries one or two. Meaning (whether this is a gate, a note or a rule) is assigned by CODE from the reference, not by the model.

duration_limit.description: The maximum length of a single stay: `2 tim`, `30 min`.

time_windows.description: Windows on the panel. There may be several with different day classes: `8-18` and `(8-15)` on one plate are two windows.

day_class.description: unspecified - no days are stated; all_days - the explicit token `alla dagar`; weekday/eve/red - the class given by how the number is set; named_weekday - a weekday is named. unspecified and all_days are DIFFERENT values: computing the complement rests on that difference.

named_weekday.description: Filled in only when day_class = named_weekday. This is a LITERAL: the holiday calendar does not apply to it - a `Tisdag 18-24` prohibition holds on a Tuesday that is a holiday.

week_parity.description: The parity of the ISO week number: `jamna veckor` even, `udda veckor` odd. This is how street cleaning is marked in Sweden: the prohibition applies every other week rather than every week. Without this field the product treats the prohibition as always in force and overstates strictness; worse, on a permitting window it would overstate permission.

dates.description:
Dates bounding the window. `mode: only` - the window applies ONLY within these ranges; `mode: except` - it applies always EXCEPT within them. A range is given as a day and month without a year (`MM-DD`) and may straddle the end of the year: `11-01` ... `05-15` is winter. A single day is written as a range whose start equals its end.

This is how the plates are written: `Galler ej 1 juli - 31 juli` is `except` with a range across July, `1 nov-15 maj` is `only` with a winter range, and `Galler ej 15/6 15/8` is `except` with two single-day ranges.

fee.description: A fee is stated on the panel (`Avgift`).

payment_method.description: What must be **shown** for the stay to be lawful: a ticket or a parking disc. This is a condition of parking, not a means of payment. The payment channel (app, SMS, machine) is out of scope: it answers no part of whether one may park here and on what terms.

permit_required.description: A special permit is required (`Sarskilt P-tillstand erfordras`).

scope_shift.description: A scope-shift token: `Ovrig tid` and the like. It means that what follows refers to the complement of the declared window. An unrecognised shift token is grounds for refusal: without it there is no telling what time the following lines refer to.

eligibility.description: Who the sign designates the spaces for. This is a CAPTION to the regime, not a check: the product does not know who is standing at the sign, and never decides whether the reader belongs to the category.

vehicle_class.description: Appears only where the sign NARROWS the range. The absence of the field means the range is not narrowed: a lone P permits parking for every registered motor vehicle, and a car must not be substituted here.

arrow.description: The extent arrow: which stretch relative to the sign the instruction above it applies to. There is no separate boundary meaning - an arrow pointing down means the stretch ends at the sign.

place_count.description: A number of spaces (`2 platser`). This is a count, not a duration: its nearest neighbour in writing is `2 tim`.

stretch_metres.description: The stretch over which the sign applies (`0-25 m`).

placement.description: A requirement about how to stand: only within a marked bay, or the arrangement shown by a pictogram.

prohibition.description: A prohibition symbol on the panel. Within its own window a prohibition OVERRIDES permission rather than being weighed equally with it.

pictogram.description: The pictogram on the panel, if there is one. A panel may carry an instruction with no text at all.

operator.description: An operator's information plate: name and telephone. States no rule, does not enter the engine, and does not lower the confidence.

tariff_code.description: A tariff number (`Taxa 13`). Set by the municipality and does not affect the reading: it is shown verbatim and does not lower the confidence.

area_code.description: The zone code for paying through an app (`Omradeskod 31370`).

uninterpreted.description: Lines the model read but assigned to no category. Shown to the user verbatim and not part of the computation.

permits_parking.description: The plate itself shows a parking sign (`P Avgift`, `P Forhyrda platser`) and thereby restores permission within its own scope. Needed where the main sign is a prohibition: photograph 019 carries a 7-18 prohibition, and `ovrig tid` permits parking again for a fee. Without this field the prohibition would extend to the complement as well.

clock.description: An hour as HH:MM, 24-hour. The model normalises `7-17` and `07-17` alike.
